Cost performance index (CPI) is the ratio of baseline costs of work performed (BCWP) to actual costs of work performed (ACWP), up to the project status date or today's date.

CPI = BCWP / ACWP

SPI (schedule performance index) shows the ratio of the budgeted cost of work performed to the budgeted cost of work scheduled.

SPI = BCWP / BCWS

CV% (cost variance percent) contains the ratio of cost variance (CV) to budgeted cost of work performed (BCWP), expressed as a percentage.  This indicates the variance between how much it should have cost to how much it has actually cost to achieve the current level of completion up to the status date or today's date

CV% = [(BCWP - ACWP) / BCWP] * 100

SV% (schedule variance percent) shows the ratio of schedule variance (SV) to budgeted cost of work scheduled (BCWS), expressed as a percentage.

SV% = (SV / BCWS) * 100

EAC (estimate at completion) contains the expected total cost of a task based on performance up to the status date.

EAC = ACWP + (Baseline cost X - BCWP) / CPI

TCPI (to complete performance index) shows the ratio of the work remaining to be done to funds remaining to be spent, as of the status date.

TCPI = (BAC - BCWP) / (BAC - ACWP)

Microsoft Project is a project management program designed to help you plan and manage your projects and communicate project information.
Whether you have a simple list of tasks or want to coordinate activities across multiple projects, Project makes it easy to get started and learn as you go.

* Seeing your tasks linked in a Gantt Chart
* Seeing how much work each person on the team has assigned to them
You can easily import this information back into Project and keep working without reentering data.
